packages.label: חֶסֶד וְגִילּוּי תּוֹרָה — דָּוִד
packages.label_en: Kindness and Torah Revelation — the David Archetype
packages.reason: Revealing Torah to others and chesed share the same essential nature: both are the outward-flowing quality of goodness ('דְּאִתְפַּשַּׁט לְבַר'). The Zohar explicitly equates chesed with outward expansion ('חֶסֶד — דְּאִתְפַּשַּׁט לְבַר'), and the Torah identifies the action of teaching Torah publicly as bechina of chesed, citing 'וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד עַל לְשׁוֹנָהּ.' David who revealed his masechet is named as the prototype of this quality. These concepts are not cause-and-effect — revealing Torah is not a consequence of chesed; they are the same thing viewed from different angles: chesed as a divine quality and revealing-Torah as its human expression.

packages.label: תּוֹרָה וְאֵשׁ
packages.label_en: Torah and Fire — the Contained Energy
packages.reason: Torah and fire share the same essential nature as an explosive, luminous, consuming force. The proof-text is Jeremiah 23: 'Is not My word like fire?' — establishing Torah as fire by explicit bechina language. This is a neutral metaphor: Torah-as-fire can be the holy teaching that illuminates, or the compressed energy that bursts into conflict when not released. In Torah #283, this bechina serves as the pivotal structural concept: the Torah kept inside (by the טוֹב-type tzaddik) is like fire imprisoned in the heart ('עֲצוּרָה בְּלִבּוֹ כְּאֵשׁ בּוֹעֶרֶת'), and it is this fire that eventually erupts as the thunderous dispute. Torah/fire is therefore the neutral causal substrate — the same energy that, when it flows outward, becomes chesed (Package 1), and when it stays hidden, produces discord (Package 3).

packages.label: מַחֲלֹקֶת וּרְעָמִים
packages.label_en: Dispute and Thunder — the Structural Metaphor
packages.reason: Dispute and thunder share the same essential nature: both are the explosive release of compressed energy. The proof is from an earlier teaching (Torah #56): 'the dispute is a bechina of thunder.' The Torah explains the physical mechanism — hot vapors absorbed by clouds until the cloud cannot contain them, splitting open as thunder — and maps it structurally onto the tzaddik-dispute: the Torah-fire (like hot vapors) is absorbed by the inward-keeping tzaddik and, when it can no longer be contained, bursts out as a dispute. מחלקת and רעמים are therefore two names for the same phenomenon — compression followed by explosive release — applied in two domains (social/spiritual and meteorological). They are not in a cause-effect chain with each other; they are co-equal bechinas of the same structural reality. The polarity is neutral: this Torah explicitly discusses both the holy dispute of tzaddikim (which IS bechina of thunder) and the wicked dispute (line 8) which is explicitly contrasted as NOT rooted in Torah. The thunder-metaphor thus describes a structure that can apply to either domain.
